d: the laws made by a government
ex: New legislation protects people who report corruption.

d: a written law passed by a parliament
ex: The statute clearly forbids the sale of land without a permit.

d: one separate part of a contract or law
ex: The contract has a clause about late payment.

d: a condition or rule inside a law or contract
ex: A provision in the law protects public workers from dismissal.

d: all the papers and records of one legal case
ex: The lawyer spent the night reading the case file.

d: a reason accepted by law for an action or claim
ex: The client had no legal ground to refuse the payment.

d: the law or rule that allows or supports an action
ex: The ministry could not explain the legal basis for the decision.

d: something that you must do by law or agreement
ex: The company has an obligation to pay its workers on time.

d: to obey a rule, law or order
ex: All suppliers must comply with the safety rules.

d: that must be obeyed by law
ex: The agreement is binding on both companies.

d: accepted by law because it is correct and official
ex: The contract is not valid without both signatures.

d: not accepted by law because it is wrong or out of date
ex: The court declared the will invalid because it was unsigned.

d: one of the people or groups in a contract or case
ex: Each party to the contract must keep its promises.

d: the rules that both sides accept in an agreement
ex: Read the terms and conditions before you sign.

d: to make a bill into a law
ex: Parliament enacted a law to protect witnesses.

d: to change the words of a law or document
ex: The parliament amended the law to include small companies.

d: a change made to a law or document
ex: The committee proposed an amendment to the third article.

d: to officially end a law
ex: The government repealed the old law on public tenders.

d: an official order made by a ruler or government
ex: A presidential decree set up the new audit office.

d: to make people obey a law or rule
ex: The police cannot enforce a law that is unclear.

d: the work of making people obey the law
ex: Law enforcement agencies shared information about the stolen goods.

d: to give someone the legal right to something
ex: This contract entitles you to thirty days of paid leave.

d: legally responsible for something
ex: The builder is liable for the damage to the roof.

d: legal responsibility for harm or debt
ex: The company denied liability for the accident.

d: failure to take proper care that causes harm
ex: The hospital was sued for negligence after the mistake.

d: the act of breaking a law, rule or agreement
ex: Late delivery is a breach of the contract.

d: failure to do what a contract says
ex: The supplier was sued for breach of contract.

d: a claim that someone did wrong, not yet proved
ex: The minister denied the allegation of corruption.

d: said to be true but not yet proved
ex: The alleged thief was seen near the shop.

d: the duty to show that a claim is true
ex: In a criminal trial, the burden of proof lies with the prosecution.

d: allowed to be used as evidence in court
ex: The judge decided that the recording was admissible.

d: not allowed to be used as evidence in court
ex: The document was inadmissible because it was a copy.

d: the right to bring a case before a court
ex: The association had no legal standing to bring the case.

d: to explain what a law or text means
ex: Judges must interpret the law, not rewrite it.

d: having more than one possible meaning
ex: The clause is ambiguous, so both sides read it differently.

d: to say the opposite of what was said before
ex: The second witness contradicted the first one.

d: to prove that a claim is wrong
ex: The lawyer refuted the claim with a bank record.

d: to mention a law or case as support
ex: The lawyer cited an earlier case to support her argument.

d: to confirm that a decision is correct
ex: The court of appeal upheld the original sentence.

d: to cancel a court decision
ex: The higher court overturned the verdict.

d: to decide that one side is right
ex: The judge ruled in favour of the tenant.

d: the steps of a case in court
ex: The court began proceedings against the supplier in March.

d: the plan or purpose to do something
ex: The prosecution must prove that he acted with intent.

d: the reason why someone commits a crime
ex: The police could not find a motive for the theft.

d: a person who helps another person commit a crime
ex: The thief and his accomplice escaped through the back door.

d: a person who commits a crime
ex: The perpetrator was identified from a camera recording.

d: allowed by law or accepted as fair
ex: Self-defence can be a legitimate reason for using force.

d: to give official permission for something
ex: Only a judge can authorise the search of a home.

d: a penalty for breaking a rule or law
ex: The company faced a heavy sanction for hiding its accounts.

d: a way the law gives to correct a wrong
ex: Compensation is the usual legal remedy for a broken contract.

d: a gap in a law that lets people avoid its rules
ex: The company used a loophole to avoid paying tax.

d: an earlier court decision used as a guide for later cases
ex: The judge followed a precedent set ten years earlier.

d: law made from the decisions of judges in earlier cases
ex: Case law shows how courts have read this article before.

d: a statement about what someone else said, not seen directly
ex: The judge refused to accept hearsay as proof.

d: indirect evidence that suggests a fact but does not prove it
ex: The case rested on circumstantial evidence only.

d: using scientific methods to investigate a crime
ex: A forensic expert examined the signature on the document.

d: an object or document shown in court as evidence
ex: The lawyer handed Exhibit A, a bank statement, to the judge.

d: a written statement that a person swears is true
ex: The manager signed an affidavit before a notary.

d: a witness's sworn statement recorded before a trial
ex: The deposition of the accountant took four hours.

d: the system of laws that controls a subject
ex: The country needs a clear legal framework for public tenders.

d: an expert lawyer's written view on a legal question
ex: The ministry asked for a legal opinion before signing.

d: having no legal effect
ex: The court declared the contract null and void.

d: a person or state that signs an agreement
ex: Every signatory to the treaty must report each year.

d: to state clearly as a condition of an agreement
ex: The contract stipulates that payment must be made within thirty days.

d: to give up a right or a rule officially
ex: He waived his right to a lawyer.

d: able to be made effective by law
ex: An oral promise is hard to make enforceable in court.

d: planned in advance
ex: The prosecutor said the attack was premeditated.

d: to cancel a decision officially
ex: The court set aside the decision because of a procedural error.

d: the freedom to decide what to do in a case
ex: Judges have discretion to reduce a sentence.

d: the official power to act given to a person or body
ex: The commission has a mandate to investigate public contracts.
